A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SynQuE/Lens research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison despite substantial reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: V3 reports original proxy-correlation and dataset-selection experiments on sentiment analysis, Text2SQL, image classification, and web navigation, together with appendix ablations.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical results and adds experiments on hybrid proxies, hallucination prompts, dataset scaling, instance-level selection, and computational cost.

M1.justification: The stated Lens aggregation changes from averaging synthetic-example scores in v3 Equation 8 to combining synthetic-as-real and real-as-synthetic scores in v4 Equations 9–10. The rubric and debiasing pipeline remains. This establishes a revision to the reported scoring rule, although v4 retains a conflicting synthetic-only description.

E1.justification: The evaluated data and downstream tasks remain financial sentiment analysis, three BIRD databases, the same 15 ImageNet classes, and 13 WebVoyager sites. Added studies reuse this coverage; dataset merging, prompt modifications, and instance-level selection vary the procedures within those tasks.

E2.justification: V4 Table 15 adds comparisons of five-proxy linear mixtures against the best individual proxies, extending beyond v3's Lens–MDM mixing analysis. The original mixing analysis and main comparator set, including MAUVE and perplexity, are retained.

E3.justification: New experimental designs include a 6^5 proxy-weight search, merging 1/2/4/8 synthetic datasets while fixing synthetic rubric samples at 200, and selecting 333 examples per class from a deduplicated pool of 29,235 instances. V4 also introduces controlled prompt comparisons and hardware-specific cost profiling. Original benchmark settings are retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds analyses of five-proxy synergy, model-dependent responses to hallucination instructions, robustness to synthetic dataset growth, instance-level selection, and computational efficiency. Earlier backbone, rubric, kernel, encoder, classifier, and real-sample sensitivity ablations remain; v3's B.9 becomes v4's B.10.

E5.justification: Five-seed averaging and correlation standard deviations are retained, with v3 Table 16 becoming v4 Table 22. V4 Table 23 extends uncertainty reporting to computational latency and Lens token usage through standard deviations. No increase in benchmark seed counts is stated.

E6.justification: Retained benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Table 15 reports hybrid Spearman correlations reaching 0.72 for sentiment and 0.89 for Movie Platform. Table 17 reports both improvements and deterioration under hallucination prompting, while Tables 18–19 and 23 add scaling, instance-selection, and cost outcomes under their respective new settings.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 replaces the ambiguous MDM expression with an explicit sum over clusters and their members, normalized by dataset size, matching the averaging procedure already described in v3 Appendix C.2. Section 4.2 also revises Lens's mathematical definition to include real-example errors. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same three central contributions: formalizing SynQuE, adapting proxy metrics, and introducing Lens with evaluation across four domains. The headline claims about selection utility and Lens on complex tasks, including the abstract's Text2SQL example, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations concerning complementary proxy weaknesses, task-dependent hybrid weights, inconsistent hallucination-prompt benefits, scaling limitations, and suitability for instance-level selection. New Practitioner Guidelines and Broader Impact sections add deployment recommendations and explain how biased real reference samples can propagate bias through selection.

D1.justification: New Tables 20–21 document dataset and rubric sizes, including website-specific counts; Appendix C.1 newly specifies balanced 150-image test sets. V4 also supplies the hallucination-prompt sentence and hardware details for cost profiling. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the retained experiments' underlying data or implementation.

R1.justification: Related work adds dataset-ranking and retrieval discussion citing Chapman, Kaushal, Kirsch, and Nadas, distinguishing SynQuE from sample selection and dataset retrieval. MAUVE is repositioned from an adapted proposed proxy to an established comparison baseline, while its evaluated computation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence are retained. V4 rewrites the proxy motivation, expands scoring explanations, introduces Practitioner Guidelines and Broader Impact sections, and updates terminology, affiliations, and cross-references. Existing appendix passages are also reorganized around their tables.

P2.justification: V4 changes typography, margins, headers, and table placement throughout. Figure 1 is redrawn and corrects its MMD exponent label. Seven tables and three pages of multipanel scatter plots are added. Figures 2–3 retain their underlying images but move and change display size.

improvement.justification: The added scaling and prompt analyses expose previously untested failure conditions, while dataset-size documentation and measured costs improve practical assessability. However, v4 revises Lens's aggregation while retaining a conflicting synthetic-only description and unchanged main results, without explaining which scoring rule those results support. This ambiguity in the central method prevents a confident judgment of the net quality improvement.
